How I work

A few principles that shape sessions and therapeutic contact.

Curiosity over judgment

We begin with steady curiosity and practical focus. Therapy is collaborative and paced to your needs.

Practical tools, thoughtful change

Sessions blend reflection with skills you can apply between meetings: grounding, boundaries, communication patterns.

Clear structure

We agree on goals, session rhythm, and regular check-ins to evaluate progress and adjust the plan.

Confidentiality & ethics

What you share is private within the limits of law and ethics. See the note on confidentiality below.

Therapeutic approach

I draw from an integrative toolkit, tailoring methods to your situation. Typical methods include:

  • {{MODALITIES}}
  • Cognitive-behavioral strategies for anxiety and mood regulation
  • Trauma-informed care and stabilizing interventions
  • Attachment-focused and relational work for couples and individuals

What people commonly worry about before starting

Below are common concerns and straightforward answers to help you decide.

Will this take forever?

Therapy is goal-oriented. Some goals are achieved in a few sessions; others take longer. We agree on metrics and revisit them regularly.

Is therapy confidential?

Yes—except where law requires disclosure (harm to self/others, abuse of a minor). I will always discuss limits of confidentiality before we begin.

I’m not sure if I’m “ill enough” for therapy.

Therapy is for growth and support, not only crisis. We will clarify whether short-term consultation or longer work fits your needs.

Do you take insurance?

Insurance policies vary. I can provide superbills for out-of-network reimbursement where appropriate; please ask during intake.

Client reflections

Reflections shared with permission; names changed for privacy.

"The sessions helped me set boundaries at work without feeling guilty. Practical and compassionate."
— A.
"I learned tools for when overwhelm hits. I appreciate the clear structure and empathy."
— M.

Helpful starter resource

Download a short intake guide that prepares you for the first session: what to expect, intake questions, and a short grounding script.

Get the Intake Guide

Reach out — request a brief consult

Complete the form below and I’ll respond within 48 business hours to arrange a 20-minute phone consult.

Confidentiality & privacy

Appointments and communications are confidential within legal and ethical limits. Records are stored securely. Please do not use email for urgent matters. See full privacy statement in the footer.

Crisis notice

If you are in crisis, at risk of harming yourself or others, or need immediate help, call 911 or your local crisis line. If you are in the United States, you can dial 988 for the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. I do not provide emergency services through this contact form.

Scope & boundaries

I provide psychotherapy for adults. I do not provide legal, medical, or forensic evaluations. If specialized assessment or higher levels of care are needed, I will make referrals.
